security_audit.summary: The high eval finding is a false positive because the file uses eval to mean an evaluation step in prose. Most markdown backtick findings are benign, but the skill does instruct agents to run bundled Python scripts and package local folders. A reference file also recommends mandatory activation language, which is a high-risk prompt-steering pattern.

remediation.suggestion: Remove mandatory activation wording or clearly mark it as opt-in research guidance. Avoid prompts that pressure agents to bypass normal tool selection.
State what each script does before execution and require user confirmation when scripts create files or inspect local paths.
Exclude hidden files, symlinks, and common secret files. Show a file manifest before writing the .skill archive.

content.value_statement: Skill authors need repeatable guidance to design skills that trigger correctly and package cleanly. This skill provides structure rules, starter scripts, validation steps, and review patterns for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains SKILL.md frontmatter requirements and trigger descriptions.
Provides init_skill.py to create a skill skeleton with resource folders.
Provides verify.py to check frontmatter, name format, and trigger wording.
Provides package_skill.py to validate and create a .skill archive.
Documents progressive disclosure, resource organization, and two-stage review patterns.
limitations: Does not create production-ready domain logic without author edits.
Packaging depends on a quick_validate module available at runtime.
Generated templates include TODO placeholders that authors must replace.
The activation reference uses forceful prompt wording that teams should review.

use_cases.title: Scaffold a new skill
use_cases.description: Create a starter SKILL.md and resource folders before adding domain content.

use_cases.title: Review skill structure
use_cases.description: Check frontmatter, trigger wording, resource organization, and validation steps before sharing a skill.

use_cases.title: Package a finished skill
use_cases.description: Validate a skill folder and build a distributable .skill archive for testing or release.

prompt_templates.title: Plan My First Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the creating-skills guidance to plan a new skill for [workflow]. Ask for missing details before drafting the structure.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Trigger Conditions
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me write clear trigger conditions for a skill about [task]. Include when to use it and when not to use it.

prompt_templates.title: Add Resources And Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my skill plan and recommend scripts, references, assets, and validation checks that are necessary for reliable use.

prompt_templates.title: Audit And Package A Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill folder for trigger quality, resource scope, validation readiness, and packaging risks. Then prepare release steps.

output_examples.input: I need a skill for reviewing API changes.
output_examples.output: A concise skill plan with trigger conditions, required references, validation steps, and clear boundaries for when the skill should activate.

output: Resource files that are useful or unnecessary.
Packaging risks to review before sharing.

output_examples.output: A shorter trigger-focused description that states when to use the skill, when not to use it, and the expected task context.

best_practices: Keep the skill description focused on when the skill should activate.
Move long guidance into references and load it only when needed.
Run validation before packaging or sharing a skill.
anti_patterns: Do not put unrelated README, changelog, or installation files into the skill.
Do not summarize the full workflow inside the trigger description.
Do not reuse forceful activation wording without reviewing policy and user experience.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create AI agent skills with SKILL.md instructions, optional resources, validation, and packaging steps.

faq.question: Does it write the final domain content for me?
faq.answer: It creates structure and guidance, but authors must add accurate domain knowledge and task-specific resources.

faq.question: Can it validate an existing skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled validator checks frontmatter, name format, trigger wording, and presence of scripts/verify.py.

faq.question: Can it package a skill for distribution?
faq.answer: Yes. The packager creates a .skill archive after validation, but authors should review included files first.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report marks it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What should teams review before reuse?
faq.answer: Teams should review bundled scripts, archive contents, and the forceful activation guidance before adopting it.
